question: Why Did Domino's Change Its Pizza Recipe?
quick_answer: Domino's changed its pizza recipe around 2009 and 2010 because its own research showed many customers thought the pizza tasted bland or poor. Instead of hiding it, Domino's ran a bold campaign openly admitting the old pizza fell short, then relaunched with a reworked crust, sauce and cheese. The honest 'we listened and fixed it' approach became a famous marketing turnaround.
key_facts: Domino's publicly admitted customers disliked the old pizza
The crust, sauce and cheese were all reworked
The honest relaunch campaign became a famous marketing case study
It helped drive a major sales and brand turnaround

body.heading: Customers did not love the old pizza
body.text: By the late 2000s, Domino's own feedback and taste tests showed that a lot of customers found the pizza disappointing, with complaints about the crust and overall flavor. Rather than quietly tweaking it, the company decided to overhaul the recipe and be open about why.

body.heading: An unusually honest relaunch
body.text: In 2009 and 2010, Domino's launched a campaign that openly shared the harsh customer criticism and admitted the old pizza needed fixing. It then introduced a reworked pizza with a new crust, sauce and cheese. Publicly admitting your product was not good enough was a bold, unusual move for a big brand.

body.heading: Why it worked
body.text: The honesty got attention and made the improvement believable. Combined with a stronger focus on technology and delivery, the recipe relaunch helped fuel a major turnaround in sales and reputation for Domino's, and it is still cited as a classic marketing example.
